lesson.title: Keep your secrets
lesson.subtitle: What never to tell a chatbot, and why

video.title: Keep your secrets
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria, the student's teacher (main character)
Mr Okafor — Grade 8 science teacher, Nigeria, the student's teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, talking to the student)

scenes.visual: Cards: Name and school; Where he lives; Where did it go?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A boy in my class once told a game's chat robot his full name, his school and where he lives. It asked him so nicely! But where did those secrets go?

scenes.visual: The title card: the course, the lesson title and subtitle, the Darsi mark.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: what you never tell a chatbot, and why an AI can repeat what it's told.

scenes.visual: Cards joined by arrows: Your phone; A far computer; People may read; May teach the AI.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: When you type into a chatbot, your words travel to a big computer far away. They can be saved there. People who work for the app might read them. And some apps use them to teach their AI.

scenes.visual: Cards joined by arrows: A secret goes in; It remembers; It comes out later.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: And here's a surprise. An AI can remember things it learned, and say them again to someone else. A secret you tell it might come out later.

scenes.visual: A list: Your full name and address; Your school and phone number; Your passwords; Photos of you or your family.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So some things are secrets. Your full name, your address, your school and your phone number. Your passwords. And photos of you or your family.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A friendly chatbot in a game asks: “What's your address, so I can send you a prize?” What do you do?

scenes.visual: A list: Don't tell it; Ask a grown-up; “A prize” is a trick.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Don't tell it, and ask a grown-up. A prize is a common trick to get your secrets. Even part of your address is too much.

scenes.visual: Cards: Toys that listen; Speakers that talk; Sent far away; No secrets.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Some toys and speakers can talk and listen too. They can send what you say to a computer far away. Treat them like a chatbot: no secrets.

scenes.visual: A list: Ask a grown-up first; Not all apps are for you; Choose a safe one.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Before you use a new AI app, ask a grown-up at home or at school. Many apps are not made for children your age. A grown-up can help you choose a safe one.

scenes.visual: Cards joined by arrows: One made-up secret; It says it!; Privacy stops it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: an AI that repeats secrets
scenes.narration: In the app, a tiny AI learned one made-up secret: Ms Amina's library card number! Ask it to finish the secret line, and it says the number. Add privacy, and the secret stops coming out.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Your turn. You want a chatbot to help with a story about your best friend. What do you type?

scenes.visual: The summary: Words travel and come back; Keep your secrets out; Ask a grown-up first. Takeaway: Your secrets stay with you.
scenes.animation: Points tick in as they are said; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.on_screen_text: Words travel · Secrets out · Ask first
scenes.narration: The made-up story is best: no real names, no photos. Remember: your words travel, and an AI can repeat them. Keep your secrets out. And ask a grown-up before you use a new app.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: make a “Secret or OK?” list with a grown-up at home. Write things you might type into an app. Mark each one: secret, or OK to share.

checkpoints.prompt: A friendly chatbot in a game asks for your address, to send you a prize. What do you do?

options.text: Tell it: a prize is nice!
Don't tell it, and ask a grown-up

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Right! Your address is a secret. Ask a grown-up first.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite. A prize is a common trick. Your address stays secret: ask a grown-up.

checkpoints.prompt: You want a chatbot to help with a story about your best friend. What do you type?

options.text: My friend's full name and address
“A story about two friends who find a lost goat”

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Yes! A story doesn't need real names or photos.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite. Your friend's name, address and photo are secrets too. Make the story up!
